cards.front: Transvaginal cervical length ≤25 mm at [___] weeks defines a 'short cervix' and substantially raises spontaneous preterm birth risk.
cards.context:
Use transvaginal ultrasound to confirm suspected short cervix. In the current WA pathway, low-risk screening starts with transabdominal assessment at the 18-20-week anatomy scan.

If transabdominal length is under 35 mm, confirm transvaginally. A confirmed 21-25 mm prompts vaginal progesterone and repeat scanning; shorter measurements need specialist review.

cards.front: Newborn blood spot screening is performed at [___] hours by heel prick; a positive screen is not a diagnosis and needs confirmatory testing.
cards.context:
The Australian Newborn Bloodspot (Guthrie) is performed at 48-72 h by heel prick — timing matters because metabolic markers (e.g., phenylalanine in PKU) rise only after milk feeding starts, but before discharge.

Coverage 25+ conditions: endocrine (congenital hypothyroidism, CAH), metabolic (PKU, MCAD, MSUD), haemoglobin (sickle, thalassaemia), CF, immunodeficiency (SCID), neuromuscular disease (SMA).

~1/800 has a positive screen. Document consent; results return ~10-14 days later.

cards.front: Intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis for women with risk factors is given to reduce neonatal [___].
cards.context:
The organism is already in the birth canal. Labour and birth are when the baby meets it, so the antibiotic is timed to that passage rather than to a clinic visit.

The effect claimed is fewer babies with early-onset group B streptococcal disease. It is prophylaxis for the newborn, not treatment of a maternal fever.

cards.front: Severe-range hypertension in pregnancy: SBP ≥[___] or DBP ≥110 mmHg; treat urgently to reduce maternal stroke risk.
cards.context:
Severe-range HTN in pregnancy (SBP ≥160 or DBP ≥110) is a hypertensive emergency — cerebral autoregulation breaks down, vasculature can't constrict adequately.

Treat acutely: IV hydralazine 5-10 mg, IV labetalol 20 mg (avoid in asthma), or oral nifedipine IR 10 mg — repeat q15-30 min until BP <160/110.

Don't aim for normotension: a precipitous drop collapses pressure-dependent uteroplacental perfusion, causing fetal distress. Target SBP 140-150, DBP 90-100 first hours, then oral (methyldopa, labetalol, nifedipine SR).

cards.front: A woman with no previous miscarriages attends an early pregnancy clinic with bleeding and a confirmed viable intrauterine pregnancy. Progesterone is not offered: for threatened miscarriage it is reserved for women with [___] or more previous miscarriages.
cards.context:
For a threatened miscarriage, when she has had no more than one miscarriage, progesterone supplementation is not recommended.

It makes little to no difference to live birth, stillbirth, or preterm birth.

cards.front: Outpatient pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) empirical antibiotics: [___] (gonorrhoea) + doxycycline (chlamydia) + metronidazole (anaerobes).
cards.context:
PID is polymicrobial (Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, Mycoplasma genitalium, anaerobes); empirical antibiotics must cover all: ceftriaxone (gonorrhoea) + doxycycline (chlamydia) + metronidazole (anaerobes).

Threshold to treat is deliberately low (CDC): any sexually active woman with pelvic pain + cervical motion tenderness OR uterine tenderness OR adnexal tenderness — start treatment.

Most managed as outpatients (oral, review at 72 h); admit for IV if pregnant, severe, suspected tubo-ovarian abscess, no response to oral, or unable to tolerate oral. Sexual partner notification + treatment essential.

cards.front: Constipation in pregnancy is largely caused by [___] slowing gut transit.
cards.context:
Progesterone relaxes smooth muscle throughout the body. In the gut this slows transit and loosens the lower oesophageal sphincter.

The same relaxation of the ureters contributes to their dilatation in pregnancy.

cards.front: EPDS interpretation thresholds: a total score of 13 is the cut-off for probable depression (full psychiatric assessment); scores of 10-12 are possible cases (repeat in 2-4 weeks); a positive response on the dedicated [___] item triggers immediate safety assessment regardless of total score.
cards.context:
EPDS is a 10-item self-report questionnaire (scored 0-30) validated for antenatal + postnatal screening.

Interpretation: <10 = low risk, routine follow-up; 10-12 = possible, repeat in 2-4 weeks; ≥13 = probable, full psychiatric assessment.

cards.front: When two or more repeat bloodspot indications apply, besides the routine sample, a [___] decides the collection timing.
cards.context:
Transfusion, birth weight under 1500 g, and unmet milk-feed criteria each have a different repeat interval. The routine spot at 48–72 hours still stands.

The guideline does not add those clocks into one date. If two or more extra indications apply, a neonatologist sets the timing.

cards.front: The main hormone of the corpus luteum, which prepares the endometrium for implantation, is [___].
cards.context:
After ovulation the emptied follicle fills with lutein cells and becomes the corpus luteum. Its progesterone turns the endometrium secretory and ready for implantation.

Without hCG from a pregnancy, it regresses after about two weeks and the progesterone fall triggers menstruation.

cards.front: Pre-eclampsia diagnosis: HTN >20 weeks plus proteinuria (≥300 mg/24h or spot urine protein:creatinine ratio ≥[___] mg/mmol) OR end-organ dysfunction.
cards.context:
2018 ISSHP/SOMANZ expanded the pre-eclampsia definition — older 'HTN + proteinuria' missed ~20% of cases.

Spot PCR has largely replaced 24-hour collection — same accuracy, far more practical. The end-organ criterion catches 'pre-eclampsia without proteinuria' cases missed by the older definition.

cards.front: Pelvic pain from altered nociception, without clear tissue damage or a somatosensory lesion, is [___] pain.
cards.context:
Nociceptive pain comes from actual or threatened damage to tissue. Neuropathic pain comes from a lesion or disease of the sensory nerves.

This third pattern is a more sensitive warning system. Pain continues although no new tissue damage is found, which is why another laparoscopy may not help.

cards.front: Postnatal mood spectrum: baby blues peak at days 3-5 and self-resolve; postnatal depression peaks at 3-6 months. Screen with [___].
cards.context:
Postnatal mood disorders form a clinical spectrum and are separated by timing, severity and loss of reality testing.

Baby blues (70-80%, days 3-5, self-limiting tearfulness) — reassurance, support, monitoring.

Postnatal depression usually emerges later, often around 3-6 months, and is screened with the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS).

cards.front: A one-sided postnatal calf larger than the other leg by more than [___] is listed as a deep vein thrombosis feature.
cards.context:
Swelling after birth is often mild and on both sides. The flowchart marks thrombosis when one calf is larger by more than 2 cm, with pain, warmth or pitting.

The same row includes prominent superficial veins. Those veins do not make a separate harmless diagnosis when the calf is also swollen.

The table says a calf or thigh increase particularly if 2 cm or more. A difference of more than 2 cm meets both wordings.

cards.front: Pre-eclampsia diagnosis requires hypertension after [___] weeks PLUS new organ involvement (renal, hepatic, haematological, neurological, pulmonary, or placental).
cards.context:
2018 ISSHP/SOMANZ broadened pre-eclampsia from 'HTN + proteinuria' to 'HTN + ANY new organ involvement' — ~20% of pre-eclampsia has no significant proteinuria but still has organ dysfunction.

Organ systems to screen at every visit after 20 weeks: renal (urinalysis, creatinine), hepatic (LFTs), haematological (FBC, haemolysis film), neurological (visual, headache, hyperreflexia), pulmonary (oedema, dyspnoea).

cards.front: The baby of an HBsAg-positive mother gets hepatitis B vaccine plus hepatitis B [___] at birth.
cards.context:
Immunoglobulin gives ready-made antibody straight away; the vaccine starts the baby making its own.

Both are given as soon as possible after birth, ideally within 12 hours, in different thighs. The baby then completes the routine hepatitis B schedule.

cards.front: Substance use in pregnancy requires a [___] approach with harm reduction; abrupt cessation of opioids or benzodiazepines is dangerous.
cards.context:
Abrupt opioid cessation in pregnancy precipitates withdrawal in mother and fetus, risking fetal distress and preterm labour. Abrupt benzo cessation risks maternal seizures.

Frame as non-judgemental harm reduction — women who feel judged stop attending antenatal care.

cards.front: ECV for breech is offered from 36 weeks (nulliparous) or 37 weeks (multiparous); overall success ~[___]%.
cards.context:
ECV is manual rotation of breech baby to cephalic by abdominal manipulation. Done at 36-37 weeks (earlier baby may turn back, later uterus too tight + fluid too low); 36w threshold for nulliparous, 37w for multiparous.

Success ~50% overall, ~70% with multiparity/posterior placenta/adequate liquor (DVP >3 cm)/non-engaged breech/operator experience.

After successful ECV, baby usually stays cephalic; failed ECV → planned CS at 39 weeks.

cards.front: Initial neonatal CPAP for this indication uses a pressure of [___] and a gas flow of 6–8 L/minute.
cards.context:
A pressure of 5 cmH2O is where CPAP is ceased after stability in an oxygen fraction of 0.21. It is not the pressure used to begin.

The same order leaves an orogastric tube, 6–8F, on free drainage. Oxygen is aimed at a preductal saturation of 92–98% at term, or 90–95% if preterm.
